title: One way to register and cycle surface looks: a look registry on ModelScene that every 3D scene extends, replacing SurfaceShading plus the ShaderMode tools set by hand
user-messages:
> 1. Surface “looks” (SurfaceShading: default, clay, curvature). This is how the shading options are registered today:
> 
> SurfaceShading.java is an enum whose position number becomes the shadingStyle uniform in mesh.fs.
> MeshNodeViewerScene, which RingScene extends, holds the current look. It binds M to cycle the looks and H to toggle the headlight, and setSurfaceLook() also switches the palette.
> ixdar-cli shading and multiview --shading look a value up by name with SurfaceShading.named().
> Adding CREASE there looks natural, but it doesn’t fit. mesh.fs gets no per-vertex data: curvature is worked out from the screen image. So the crease field would need a new vertex attribute in the shared lit shader.
> 
> 2. The heat-map mode (ShaderMode.SCALAR). This one already exists:
> 
> HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.java:699 has setPerVertexScalar(values, min, max). It uploads one float per vertex as attribute 3, and the mesh_scalar shaders colour it with the palette’s scalar ramp.
> The only user is EmbeddedTMeshScene’s refinement density map. That is the same pattern a crease view needs: set the mode to SCALAR, then upload the values.

I want one way to register looks and one way to cycle them,  and the ring scene to register view
ok create a ticket and worktree and get started
description:
Today three knobs decide how a mesh surface is coloured and they fight:
- SurfaceShading (default, clay, curvature), owned by MeshNodeViewerScene, cycled by M, set by `ixdar-cli shading` and `multiview --shading`; its ordinal is mesh.fs's shadingStyle uniform.
- HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.ShaderMode (LAMBERT, STAGES, SCALAR, TEXTURED; FLAT, CREST_VS_BOUNDARY and MSC are never set by anything), set directly by RegionLayer, ConnectionTool, RingRegionTool, MeshNodeViewerScene (textures, edge-mark overlay), MeshBooleanScene and EmbeddedTMeshScene (the SCALAR density map), each saving and restoring the mode it replaced.
- In HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.render, any non-default SurfaceShading overrides the ShaderMode, so clay and the scalar heat map never combine, and the scalar shader (mesh_scalar.fs) is unlit.

Wanted: one way to register looks and one way to cycle them, with scenes registering their own.

1. A SurfaceLook type replacing the SurfaceShading enum: a name and one-line description, a colour source (solid, per-face groups, texture, or a per-vertex field shown as a ramp), a lighting (default, clay, curvature), the palette it wears, and optional enter/leave hooks.
2. A registry on ModelScene (the parent of every 3D scene; each fills ModelScene.runtime through createRuntime()): `setLooks(List<SurfaceLook>)` overridden down the hierarchy like setTools/setControls, super first so default, clay and curvature lead; called once from initGL. M cycles the list; `setLook(name)` is the only way to change it and applies it to ModelScene.runtime. RingScene registers regions and parts; EmbeddedTMeshScene its split-density map; MeshBooleanScene textured.
3. One lit shader: mesh_scalar.fs folds into mesh.fs as a per-vertex field channel (attribute 3, a constant when unset) that a look applies either as a colour ramp or as darkening over the base colour, under any lighting. The capturedLook override goes away. The darkening mode is what VIEW-29's crease overlay feeds; that ticket stays separate.
4. Callers stop calling setShaderMode: the region layer, G, the region tool and the connection tool select the regions or parts look and remember the look they replaced; per-face draw ranges stay (they hide faces and carry exploded-view offsets) but no longer decide the colour. The dead modes are deleted.
5. Automation: `ixdar-cli shading` and `multiview --shading` resolve names against the active scene's registry and refuse an unknown name with the scene's list; ui-state lists the looks; both routes work in every ModelScene, not only MeshNodeViewerScene.
6. Keys: RingScene binds H to show/hide rings and MeshNodeViewerScene binds H to the headlight, so the ring scene lists two H rows. The headlight becomes part of the clay and field looks' lighting rather than its own key.

Decisions taken when asked to start (2026-11-07): regions and parts are looks in the M cycle with G kept as a shortcut to regions and back; the headlight folds into the looks; the crease field is VIEW-29's darkening overlay, not a look, because the user rejected VIEW-22's replacing heat map.
definition-of-done:
1. SurfaceShading and HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.ShaderMode are gone; SurfaceLook (colour source, light, textured, paper palette, optional field) plus ModelScene.setLooks/setLook and SurfaceLooks (registered, picked, a tool's override) are the only way a scene colours its surface; no class sets a shader mode.
2. In the ring scene M cycles default, clay, curvature, regions, parts; G picks regions and back; the region tool, connection tool fills and exploded view still colour, hide and offset regions as before (multiviews on IMG_4111).
3. The split-density map in EmbeddedTMeshScene is a registered field look, drawn lit.
4. `ixdar-cli shading <name>` takes any registered look in any ModelScene and refuses an unknown name with the scene's list; `multiview --shading <name>` takes any look the mesh viewer scenes registered; ui-state reports the picked and shown look and the list.
5. Unit tests: registry order and cycle, lookup by name and refusal, override in place of the pick, field values read when shown (SurfaceLooksTest).
6. A launch entry opens IMG_4111 in the ring scene for the user to cycle M.
testing-plan:
1. Unit tests for the registry and look selection.
2. Multiview of IMG_4111 in each look, before and after, on the Mac scene host.
3. The user cycles M and toggles G in the ring scene.
changes-made: Built: SurfaceLook replaces SurfaceShading and ShaderMode; SurfaceLooks holds the registered, picked and override look; ModelScene.setLooks (super first) and setLook, M cycles, the shown look is applied to surfaceRuntime() every frame with the paper palette. mesh_scalar folded into mesh.fs as colour source FIELD under any light; FLAT, CREST_VS_BOUNDARY and MSC removed; feature edges draw whenever set. RegionLayer and ConnectionTool set looks.override instead of shader modes; G picks the regions look. Differences from the plan: the field channel only ramps (VIEW-29 adds its darkening when it has a user); the headlight stays a flag on ixdar-cli shading and multiview, with the viewer's H key removed (it clashed with the ring scene's H); multiview still needs a mesh viewer scene for its selection framing.

Reworked after review: each look is one line where the scene offers it, new SurfaceLook(id, description, colour, light, palette) or new SurfaceLook(id, description, light, field), as each control is one ControlHint line; ModelScene registers default, textured, clay, curvature in setTools, RingScene adds regions and parts, EmbeddedTMeshScene split_density. Code picks and overrides looks by id (setLook(id), looks.override(id), looks.clearOverride(id)), with the ids as constants beside the control ids (ModelScene.DEFAULT_LOOK, TEXTURED_LOOK, RingScene.REGIONS_LOOK, PARTS_LOOK). The palette is named in the line (Palettes.PAPER for clay and curvature) instead of a paper flag. Texture is its own colour source: the default look never samples it, the textured look does; MeshBooleanScene picks textured for a UV bundle as it did before. The repair fills reuse the regions look.

Switching between a dark and a paper look stalled the frame ~0.45 s on IMG_4111. A flight recording on the Mac (20 flips, 620 render-thread samples) put 94% in RegionLayer.resolveLabels -> MeshLabels.resolve -> RingRegions.nearestActiveFace: a palette swap re-resolved every part label's points with a scan of all 981k faces, though only the colours depend on the palette. MeshLabels.recolour now colours the labels as last resolved, and the region layer's palette branch calls it instead; after the fix the same 20 flips took 32 samples and every switch costs what a same-palette switch does (0.8-0.97 s for ten frames against 1.21-1.40 s before). MeshLabelsTest checks recolouring matches resolving again in the new palette.
review-summary: Every model scene now registers its surface looks in one list that M cycles and tools override, replacing SurfaceShading and hand-set shader modes. Looks, shader modes and tool colouring used to fight, so no scene could add looks such as the ring scene's regions and parts.
